### (a) A genuine retrieval weakness

Code-concept queries that use performance vocabulary get pulled toward the *prose that
discusses* GPU behaviour instead of the script that implements it. "Where is GPU memory
sampled repeatedly while a job is running?" retrieves the results documents, not
`vram_watch.ps1`. This corpus is unusually prose-heavy — every results document talks
about the code — so the embedding space is crowded with near-duplicate statements about
the same subsystems.

content:
### Two GPU-specific caveats for later phases

1. **Usable VRAM is not 12 GB.** Windows/WDDM reserves memory for the desktop. Even with
   `nvidia-smi` showing `Compute Mode: Default` and nothing heavy running, only ~11.0 GB was
   allocatable. Budget **~10.5–11.0 GB usable**, not 12227 MiB.
2. **WDDM shared-memory spill is a real benchmarking hazard.** `nvidia-smi -q` reports a
   16384 MiB "shared" pool of which only 28 MiB was free. Under WDDM, CUDA can silently
   spill into system RAM instead of failing with OOM, which would make benchmark numbers look
   plausible while actually running far slower. **All later benchmarks must record VRAM
   alongside tokens/s** so a spill is detectable.
3. Per-process VRAM attribution is unavailable under WDDM ("Not available in WDDM driver
   model"), so VRAM accounting must be done as a global delta, not per process.

### 4.3 GPU utilisation and VRAM — the offload proof

Measured with `scripts/vram_watch.ps1` (`nvidia-smi` sampled every 300–500 ms) during sustained
inference. Raw: `benchmarks/vram_gpu_full_99.csv`, `benchmarks/vram_cpu_only.csv`.

| Metric | GPU full offload (`-ngl 99`) | CPU only (`-ngl 0`) |
|---|---|---|
| Peak VRAM used | **3,257 MiB** | 2,684 MiB |
| Mean GPU utilisation | **22.3 %** | 6.2 % |
| **Peak GPU utilisation** | **94 %** | 49 % (ambient desktop, not the model) |
| **Peak board power** | **139.19 W** (at the 140 W cap) | 70.47 W |
| Peak SM clock | 2,700 MHz | 2,700 MHz |
| Throughput (tg) | 490.5 t/s | 91.9 t/s |

Idle baseline for reference: ~2011–2116 MiB VRAM, 4–6 % utilisation, ~20 W.

**Why this proves real GPU compute (requirement #8):**

1. **GPU utilisation climbs to 94 %** during offloaded inference vs 6.2 % mean on CPU — the
   GPU is doing work, not idling as a display adapter.
2. **Board power hits the 140 W cap** (139.19 W) versus ~20 W idle — sustained compute-level draw.
3. **Throughput is 5.3× higher** than CPU and is **invariant to host thread count**, the
   signature of GPU-bound execution.
4. Backend diagnostics explicitly report `compute capability 12.0` and
   `loaded CUDA backend from …ggml-cuda.dll`.

**Honest caveat on the VRAM delta.** Peak VRAM rose to 3257 MiB against a ~2011–2116 MiB
baseline — an apparent delta of ~1150 MiB for a 610 MB model. The extra is the CUDA context,
compute buffers and KV cache (4096-ctx f16 KV for this architecture is ~450 MB), not the model
alone. The CPU-only run also showed ambient peaks (2684 MiB) caused by unrelated desktop
applications, since Windows gives no per-process VRAM attribution under WDDM. **Model-resident
VRAM was confirmed directly instead:** with `llama-server` loaded, VRAM read 3293 MiB, and
after shutdown it returned to **2023 MiB** — i.e. the model + runtime were genuinely released.

# vram_watch.ps1 - sample GPU VRAM/utilisation while a workload runs.
# Phase 1/2 helper for the Local AI Coprocessor project.
#
# Writes each sample to the CSV immediately rather than buffering until the end.
# That matters: an earlier version accumulated rows and only wrote on completion, so
# when the watcher was stopped early (or the parent was killed) the whole series was
# lost and a stability run had no VRAM evidence at all.
#
# Usage: pwsh -File vram_watch.ps1 -Seconds 30 -IntervalMs 500 -OutFile logs\vram.csv

param(
  [int]$Seconds = 30,
  [int]$IntervalMs = 500,
  [string]$OutFile = ''
)

$deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($Seconds)
$first = $true
$count = 0
$peakMem = 0; $peakUtil = 0; $sumUtil = 0; $peakPwr = 0.0; $peakClk = 0
$writer = $null

if ($OutFile) {
  $dir = Split-Path -Parent $OutFile
  if ($dir -and -not (Test-Path $dir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null }
  # truncate and write the header up front so the file is valid even if we are killed
  'time,gpu_util,mem_used_mb,mem_total_mb,temp_c,power_w,sm_clock_mhz' |
    Set-Content -Path $OutFile -Encoding UTF8
}

while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
  $line = & nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu,power.draw,clocks.sm --format=csv,noheader,nounits 2>$null
  if ($line) {
    $p = $line -split ',\s*'
    $util = [int]$p[1]; $mem = [int]$p[2]; $pwr = [double]$p[5]; $clk = [int]$p[6]
    $count++
    if ($mem -gt $peakMem) { $peakMem = $mem }
    if ($util -gt $peakUtil) { $peakUtil = $util }
    if ($pwr -gt $peakPwr) { $peakPwr = $pwr }
    if ($clk -gt $peakClk) { $peakClk = $clk }
    $sumUtil += $util

    if ($OutFile) {
      # append immediately, flushing every sample
      "$($p[0]),$util,$mem,$([int]$p[3]),$([int]$p[4]),$pwr,$clk" |
        Add-Content -Path $OutFile -Encoding UTF8
    }
  }
  Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $IntervalMs
}

if ($count -gt 0) {
  Write-Output "samples            : $count"
  Write-Output "peak VRAM used     : $peakMem MiB"
  Write-Output "peak GPU util      : $peakUtil %"
  Write-Output "avg GPU util       : $([math]::Round($sumUtil/$count,1)) %"
  Write-Output "peak power         : $peakPwr W"
  Write-Output "peak SM clock      : $peakClk MHz"
  if ($OutFile) { Write-Output "raw samples        : $OutFile" }
} else {
  Write-Output "no samples collected"
}
